subject: MAX function
notes: VERDICT UPHELD, on stronger evidence than the original, with one citation corrected. CITATION FIX: the original note said '§8.8.4.2.2 makes two greatest-valued numeric arguments equal in algebraic value'; §8.8.4.2.2 is 'General format' and --check FAILS on that text. The clause is §8.8.4.2.4 (--check OK: 'For operands whose class is numeric, a comparison is made with respect to the algebraic value of the operands regardless of the manner in which their usage is described ... Zero is considered a unique value regardless of the sign'). WHY THIS SURVIVES THE ATTACK AT IMPLEMENTATION LEVEL RATHER THAN BY SAMPLING: leftmost-wins is a property of ExtremeIndex ALONE - `for (int i = 1; i < xs.Length; i++) { int c = cmp(xs[i], xs[k]); if (max ? c > 0 : c < 0) k = i; }` - and is independent of the comparator passed in, so it holds identically for all six MaxString/MinString overloads (native pad-compare, the ushort[] alphanumeric-PCS weights, and the NationalCollation variant) and for OrdMaxString/OrdMinString, which is the whole family in one place. The original evidence only exhibited SAME-CONTENT / DIFFERENT-LENGTH ties, which cannot distinguish leftmost-wins from a stable comparator; the refuter added a tie between DIFFERENT CONTENTS of EQUAL VALUE, which is what the rule is actually about, and it passes on the weights overload. The NUMERIC/INDEX half remains vacuous rather than unverified, and the argument is sound: §8.8.4.2.4 makes two greatest-valued numeric arguments equal in algebraic value (and makes signed and unsigned zero one value), §15.59.4 r3 confines the SIZE question to alphanumeric and national, and under standard arithmetic §15.4.1 puts the returned value in a mode-defined intermediate data item whose characteristics come from the mode rather than from the selected argument - so two tied numeric or index arguments have no observable difference in content to choose between. CONTINGENCY WORTH RECORDING: this rule governs which of the TIED arguments is returned; whether the tie is real is RV-15.59.4-1's question, and at the boundaries documented there the 'greatest value' premise is itself wrong. EDITION WINDOW as in AR-15.59.3-1, from Annex E only. EVIDENCE: PROBED, --std 2023. REFUTER'S DECISIVE CASE - an equal-value tie between DIFFERENT contents, on the non-identity-PCS weights overload: E:/Temp/rfmax/tiew.cob (RFMAXTIEW) `OBJECT-COMPUTER. XX PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE AL.` / `SPECIAL-NAMES. ALPHABET AL IS "A" ALSO "B", "C", "D".` with P1 PIC X VALUE "A", P2 PIC X VALUE "B" prints REL=A-EQ-B (the program's own relation condition confirms the tie is real), then `MOVE FUNCTION MAX(P1 P2) TO R1` -> T1=A and `MOVE FUNCTION MAX(P2 P1) TO R1` -> T2=B. The selection follows ARGUMENT POSITION over two operands that are equal but not identical, which is leftmost-wins in the form the rule states it. Corroborating, from the original adjudication (size-tie form): E:/Temp/pbmax/maxsize.cob `01 S3 PIC X(3) VALUE "AB". 01 S6 PIC X(6) VALUE "AB".` -> `STRING FUNCTION MAX(S3 S6) ... INTO R12` = C1=[AB |********] (size 3) and the reversed order C2=[AB    |*****] (size 6); national, E:/Temp/pbmax/maxnat3.cob `FUNCTION LENGTH(FUNCTION MAX(N3 N6))` -> L1=000C (3) and `FUNCTION LENGTH(FUNCTION MAX(N6 N3))` -> L2=000F (6); zero-length leftmost, maxzl2.cob `FUNCTION MAX("" SP)` -> Z=[|***********]. Refuter's alphabetic-item repeat, E:/Temp/rfmax/cats.cob: `FUNCTION MAX(AL1 AL2)` over PIC A(3)/PIC A(6) both VALUE "ABC" -> ALPHA1=[ABC|********], reversed -> ALPHA2=[ABC   |*****]. CONTROL: E:/Temp/rfmax/ctl.cob compiles and runs (CTLNUM=0099, CTLSTR=XYZ).
